drivingQuestion: Why teach that ratification by one party blocks nullification?
outcomeNote: the answer comes in the next unit (nedarim.sugya235)

segments.he: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁקִּיֵּים אֶחָד מֵהֶן. לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנָא? הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר הֵפֵר זֶה בְּלֹא זֶה — וְלֹא כְּלוּם, קִיֵּים אֶחָד מֵהֶן לְמָה לִי? צְרִיכָא לְמִיתְנֵי?!
segments.en: At the end of the mishna it is stated: «And needless to say,» it is not nullified «if one of them ratified» the vow. The Gemara asks: «Why do I» need the mishna «to teach» this? «Now,» it «was stated» that if «one» of them «nullified» the vow «without the other,» it «is nothing,» her vow is not nullified. If «one of them ratified» it, «why do I» need it to state that her vow is not nullified? Is it «necessary to teach» this?

moves.summary: the ratification clause is obvious a fortiori
moves.about: if nullification by one alone is ineffective, ratification by one obviously leaves the vow standing
